newsitem.title: UK: British bookmakers shorten odds on Labour govt.
newsitem.headline: British bookmakers shorten odds on Labour govt.

text.p: British bookmakers William Hill said on Thursday they had cut their odds on the opposition Labour Party winning the May 1 election to 1-8 from 1-7.
William Hill also reduced the odds of Labour winning with an overall majority to 1-6 from 2-9.
The ruling Conservatives were quoted at 9-2 to be the largest single party, out from 4-1. The government's chances of winning an overall majority is now seen as 11-1 against.
"Despite pushing the Conservative odds out to the longest in living memory we aren't taking any significant money for them whatsoever," said Hill's spokesman, Graham Sharpe.
Opinion polls put Labour 20 points or more ahead of the Conservatives. Labour needs a 4.3 percent swing in the vote from the last election, to take power.
The bookmaker offers odds of 4-1 on a hung parliament.
